University of Colorado Medicine (CU Medicine) is the region’s largest and most comprehensive multi-specialty physician group practice. The CU Medicine team delivers business operations, revenue cycle and administrative services to support the patients of over 4,000 University of Colorado School of Medicine physicians and advanced practice providers. These providers bring their unparalleled expertise at the forefront of medicine to deliver trusted, compassionate health care services at primary and specialty care clinics as well as facilities operated by affiliate hospitals of the University of Colorado.

We are seeking a motivated Coding Education Specialist
with an emphasis in Diagnostics experience to join our Coding Services department.

This job can be performed 100% remotely and out of state candidates will be considered.

The Coding Education Specialist will primarily be responsible for supporting and leading ongoing education to existing coding staff, coordination with leadership for varied projects related to team success and coder development, research of any coding related questions, and the planning and education of newly hired coders. The position is also expected to be able to assist in trending, coding analysis, coder feedback and providing education either individually or developing and presenting a group presentation.

Job Duties

Serve as a coding expert for assigned specialties.
Provide training and education to new and existing coders in conjunction with the Coding Services (CS) Department standards.
Using audits, monitor the quality of coding staff work as directed by Coding Services Management and identify areas of education.
Create and provide presentations in regard to education to the team for targeted specialty areas and coding groups.
Assist with researching coder questions and provide effective and accurate guidance.
Identify and research correct coding for new CPT codes, as well as present this information to the team.
Provide extensive education regarding any changes to ICD 10 and CPT to coding staff in adherence to regulatory guidelines that is pertinent to their assigned specialties.
Perform occasional edit analysis to identify educational opportunities and edit modification.

Requirements

CPC or AHIMA coding certification required.
3-5 years of Diagnostics coding experience with demonstrated expertise in procedural and diagnosis coding required.
Specialty certifications preferred.
Teaching physician guidelines preferred.
EMR and Practice Management software experience.
Proficient in reporting and analytics.

Case Manager – Permanent Supportive Housing | Professional I

Make a Difference Where It Matters Most

At The Centers, we believe that safe, stable housing is the foundation for every person's ability to thrive. Our Permanent Supportive Housing (PSH)
program combines low-barrier, affordable housing with integrated health care and wraparound supportive services — helping individuals and families who have experienced chronic homelessness build the stability they deserve.

We are looking for a compassionate, skilled, and mission-driven Case Manager
to join our PSH Care Team. If you are someone who believes in the dignity and resilience of every person you serve, and who brings evidence-based practice to life through genuine human connection, we want to hear from you.

What You Will Do

As a Case Manager in our Permanent Supportive Housing program, you will provide strength-based case management services to individuals with histories of chronic homelessness, behavioral health conditions, and complex psychosocial needs. Your work will be rooted in whole-person care — addressing not just immediate needs, but the medical, behavioral health, substance use, and social determinants of health factors that shape long-term wellness and housing retention.

Engagement and Client Support

You will build and sustain meaningful, therapeutic relationships with clients through face-to-face, telephonic, office-based, property-based, and community-based engagement. You will explain the purpose and process of case management to clients, conduct comprehensive assessments of strengths and needs, administer appropriate screening tools, and support clients in developing the independent living skills — including budgeting, understanding leases, and paying bills — that promote lasting housing stability.

Service Planning and Case Management

You will develop and maintain individualized service plans and housing success plans that reflect client goals, measurable outcomes, and evidence-based strategies. You will apply Housing First
, Harm Reduction
, Motivational Interviewing
, Stages of Change
, and Stage-Wise Interventions
to support wellness and housing retention. You will also provide ongoing life skills training and pro-social support, individually and in groups, and conduct continuous monitoring to evaluate progress and adjust interventions.

Coordination, Linkage, and Monitoring

You will work side-by-side with a multidisciplinary team — including counselors, nurses, physicians, pharmacists, social service staff, and Property Management — to connect clients to the full range of community resources they need: primary care, behavioral health, substance use services, benefit programs, educational supports, vocational resources, and social networks. You will assist clients with benefit applications, advocacy, and appeals, and support smooth transitions in care following hospitalizations or other disruptions.

Clinical Proficiency and Documentation

You will recognize behavioral health, physical health, and substance misuse presentations, apply appropriate risk and lethality assessment practices, and use clinical supervision effectively. You will document all case management activity in the organization's electronic medical record system in a clear, objective, and timely manner, ensuring that documentation directly links services to client goals and outcomes. You will protect client privacy and confidentiality in strict accordance with applicable laws and organizational policy.

Site and Program Support

You will contribute to the vitality of the PSH community by participating in multidisciplinary team meetings, housing inspections, move-in and move-out planning, and community-building activities. You will also support onsite food pantry operations approximately once per month and maintain required food safety certification as provided through The Centers.

What We Are Looking For

Education

High school diploma or equivalent required.
Bachelor's degree in Social Work, Psychology, or a mental health-related field preferred. If your degree is in a related field, two years of care coordination or case management experience is preferred.

Licensure and Certification

Valid Ohio driver's license and access to an insured vehicle required for client transportation and community-based services.
Nonviolent Crisis Intervention certification required within 60 days of hire.
Active Community Health Worker certification preferred.

Experience

At least three years of case management or care coordination experience required.
Prior experience working with adults with serious and persistent mental illness preferred.

Skills And Competencies

Ability to work collaboratively and effectively as part of a multidisciplinary team.
Ability to develop effective therapeutic relationships and engage clients in assessment, goal setting, service planning, and ongoing care coordination.
Ability to identify needs, problem-solve barriers, and connect clients to appropriate community resources and supports.
Working knowledge of behavioral health, substance use, trauma-informed care, stages of change, harm reduction, and housing stability practices.
Ability to understand and support a team-based, client-centered service delivery model.

Working Conditions

This role operates in professional office, property-based, and community-based environments throughout the Cleveland area and surrounding communities. Local travel is required to provide case management, attend meetings and trainings, transport or accompany clients, and support community-based service needs. The employee may be required to lift up to 40 pounds occasionally in connection with site, delivery, or food pantry activities. Approved nonviolent crisis intervention and de-escalation techniques are expected to be applied when needed.

Why Join The Centers?

The Centers is a community anchor — a place where dedicated professionals come to do meaningful work alongside colleagues who are equally committed to care. As a member of the PSH Care Team, you will be part of an integrated, collaborative approach that touches every aspect of a person's well-being.

The Centers is an Equal Opportunity Employer and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

Join the HJF Team!

HJF is seeking a Program Manager
to oversee a collection of related/integrated projects that together support a long-term research initiative. This position strategically guides one or more project managers and related technical staff to ensure they are all working effectively toward the program’s stated objectives. Typically oversees moderate to highly complex scope of work.

This position will provide technical and operational support to accomplish the mission of the Psychological Health Center of Excellence (PHCoE).
Located in Silver Spring, MD,the PHCoE is a Department of Defense (DoD) initiative focused on improving mental health service delivery and promoting psychological health among service members. It collaborates across the DoD, the Department of Veterans Affairs, and other agencies to develop clinical practice guidelines for psychological health conditions, substance use disorders, and suicide risk. PHCoE also produces evidence-based resources, clinical support tools, and expert-reviewed briefs to enhance patient care, operational readiness, and human performance in military settings

The Henry M. Jackson Foundation for the Advancement of Military Medicine (HJF) is a nonprofit organization dedicated to advancing military medicine. We serve military, medical, academic and government clients by administering, managing and supporting preeminent scientific programs that benefit members of the armed forces and civilians alike. Since its founding in 1983, HJF has served as a vital link between the military medical community and its federal and private partners. HJF's support and administrative capabilities allow military medical researchers and clinicians to maintain their scientific focus and accomplish their research goals.

new_jobs.description:
Position Overview

Seeking a social worker for weekend evening shifts to provide clinical social work services in a hospital emergency and inpatient setting.

Key Responsibilities

Assist patients and families with personal, family, medical, and environmental challenges.
Conduct psychosocial and risk assessments, assign diagnoses, and develop treatment plans.
Collaborate on discharge planning and outpatient services, working with healthcare teams and community agencies.

Qualifications & skills:

Master’s degree in social work.
Strong clinical skills with experience in therapeutic modalities.
Preferred experience in medical/hospital social work.
Encouraged from diverse backgrounds; Spanish skills a plus.
Licensure as LCSW in MA required; LICSW preferred.
